meta.description: Yasakia is the dating app where you talk first: an AI agent gets to know you, then opens small, mutual batches of profiles.

chrome.footer: Yasakia is an open-source product by Krizaka, made in Québec.

privacy.title: What Yasakia keeps about you, and for how long
privacy.lead: A dating app learns personal things. Here is exactly what we store, where, for how long, and how it disappears — in plain words.

sections.title: Our principles
paragraphs: We keep the least we can. Your position is rounded to about one kilometre on your phone's request, before it is written: your exact location never exists on our servers. We never read your contacts.
What the agent learns is yours to change. Your portrait — who you are, who you are looking for — can be corrected at any time, and every correction wins over what the agent guessed.
Sensitive answers are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM, a key per environment), and so is what you write in a report.
Nothing you share trains a model. Not your conversation with the agent, not your photos, not your messages — not ours, not anyone's.
No score is ever shown, and nobody sees your photos unless the two of you are in each other's batch or in an intro.

sections.title: What we store
paragraphs: Your account: your e-mail address (to send your sign-in codes), your language, your date of birth (checked once to make sure you are 18 or older; nobody else ever sees it), and when you accepted these terms.
Your profile: your first name or nickname, your gender and who you want to meet, the age range and distance you accept, what you are looking for, and your rounded position.
Your photos: re-encoded when you upload them, which removes every piece of metadata your phone added — including where the photo was taken.
Your conversation with the agent and your portrait: what you told the agent and what it understood, so the batches fit you better each time.
Your batches, decisions and debriefs: who was proposed to you, what you answered, and your debrief answers.
Your intros: the messages you exchange during an intro. The agent never reads them.
Your safety actions: the people you blocked and the reports you filed.
Your phone's notification token, so we can tell you when a batch is ready or someone wrote to you.
The cost of the agent: for each call to an AI model, its size and duration — never its content.

sections.title: Where it is kept
paragraphs: Our database and our servers run at DigitalOcean, in its Toronto region (Canada).
Photos are stored at Bunny.net and only ever served through links signed for one viewer, valid five minutes.
Sign-in codes are sent by e-mail through Mailgun. Notifications go through Expo to Apple or Google, which deliver them to your phone.

The conversation with the agent is processed by the AI model we configure: Orazaka, the sovereign AI platform built by Krizaka, or a hosted model whose contract forbids keeping or training on what it receives.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: As long as your account exists for your account, profile, portrait, conversation with the agent, batches and blocks — you can change or remove most of it from the app.
Sign-in codes: ten minutes. Data exports you ask for: 24 hours. Notification tokens: until you sign out, turn notifications off or uninstall the app.
Intro messages: as long as the intro exists; when either of you deletes their account, the intro and its messages disappear for both.
Reports are kept as long as safety reviews need them; when an account is deleted, the report no longer points to it.

When you delete your account, everything above is deleted at once, and your photos are removed from storage within 30 days at most — usually within minutes. What remains is a record that a deletion happened (a random identifier and its date), and the agent's cost figures without any link to you.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You can see, correct, export and delete your data at any time, from the app: Settings → Download my data gives you everything we hold about you as a file; Settings → Delete my account deletes it for good.

Québec's Law 25 and Europe's GDPR give you these rights and more (to object, to withdraw consent, to complain to the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec or your own authority). Write to us for anything the app does not do yet: we answer within 30 days.
Krizaka's person in charge of the protection of personal information answers through our contact form.

sections.title: Adults only
paragraphs: Yasakia is for people aged 18 and over. We check the date of birth when an account is created and close any account we learn belongs to a minor.

terms.title: The rules of Yasakia
terms.lead: Yasakia works because people are honest and kind to each other. These terms say what we expect from you, and what you can expect from us.

sections.title: Who we are
paragraphs: Yasakia is made by Krizaka, in Québec. The app is free; its code is open source under the Apache 2.0 licence.

sections.title: Who can use Yasakia
paragraphs: You must be 18 or older, use one account only, and be who you say you are: your photos show you, and only you; your name is yours.
You keep your sign-in codes to yourself. If you think someone else used your account, sign out everywhere from the settings and tell us.

sections.title: How we treat each other
paragraphs: No harassment, threats, hate, or pressure. No scams, requests for money, advertising or recruiting. No sexual content, and nothing involving a minor — ever; we report such content to the authorities.
Respect a no, a pass, or silence. An intro that fades is not a failure; insisting is.
When you meet someone, choose a public place, tell a friend, and leave whenever you want. We do not run background checks.

sections.title: The agent
paragraphs: The agent is an AI. It helps you describe yourself and opens batches of people who could suit you — both ways. It can be wrong, it never gives medical, legal or financial advice, and it never talks about other members.
Nobody pays to skip a debrief or to get a bigger batch: the rules are the same for everyone.

sections.title: Blocks, reports and sanctions
paragraphs: You can block or report anyone from their card, their profile or an intro. A block is immediate and invisible to the other person. A report is kept and reviewed; the person is never told who reported them.
We may hide a photo, freeze an intro, suspend or close an account that breaks these rules, and keep what a review needs.

sections.title: What you share
paragraphs: Your photos and words remain yours. You allow us to store them and show them to the people Yasakia introduces you to, only for as long as your account exists.

sections.title: Leaving, and the rest
paragraphs: You can pause your account or delete it at any time from the app. We may change these terms; when it matters, the app tells you before it applies.
Yasakia is provided as it is, without a promise of a match. These terms are governed by the laws of Québec and Canada.

deleteAccount.title: Delete your Yasakia account
deleteAccount.lead: You can delete your account at any time, from the app, in a few seconds. It is permanent: everything that is yours disappears.
inAppSteps: Confirm. You are signed out and your account no longer exists.
deleteAccount.withoutApp: If you no longer have the app, write to us from the e-mail address of your account through our contact form, asking us to delete it. We confirm the deletion within 30 days.
deleted: Immediately: your account, profile, rounded position, conversation with the agent and portrait, batches and debriefs, intros and their messages, blocks and notification tokens.
Within 30 days at most — usually within minutes: your photos, from our storage.
A confirmation is sent to your e-mail address.
kept: A record that a deletion happened: a random identifier and its date, nothing that identifies you.
Reports filed by or about you, for safety reviews, without any link to your account.
The cost figures of the agent's calls (size and duration, never their content), without any link to you.
deleteAccount.exportHint: Before you leave, you can download everything we hold about you: Settings → Download my data.
